=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1328-1330 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: `_request_confirmation(target.warning)` runs inside the per-target loop, so a push with multiple unknown-destination targets (e.g. `git push origin HEAD:$DEST1 HEAD:$DEST2`) prints two or more JSON objects to stdout instead of one.
  WHY: The hook harness expects exactly one structured JSON output per evaluation. Concatenated JSON objects are invalid JSON; if the harness fails to parse stdout it may fail open and allow the push.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1328-1330 and 1394-1395 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: When a push command has an unknown-destination target followed by a merged-branch target (e.g. `git push origin HEAD:$DEST feature/x` where `feature/x`'s PR is merged), the per-target `_request_confirmation` on the unknown target emits a `permissionDecision: ask` JSON object before the merged-branch target triggers a block at line 1395 (exit code 2).
  WHY: The stdout `ask` JSON cannot be retracted after the block is returned, leaving conflicting hook signals — the harness may honour the ask and allow a push to a merged branch.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1398-1402 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The post-loop bulk-reasons handling calls `_request_confirmation(...)` directly instead of combining its reason with any unknown-destination reasons that may have been deferred.
  WHY: A bulk push that also has an unknown destination can emit two separate `permissionDecision: ask` JSON objects.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1328-1330, 1394-1402 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The template copy is byte-identical to the source and has the same three defects: per-target confirmation in the loop, ask-before-block on mixed targets, and separate bulk-reasons confirmation.
  WHY: Consumer repos receive the un-batched code path via the `@stable` sync. The same invalid-output and conflicting-signal failures apply.
- tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:989-991 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The two regression tests that the LAST RUN DIFF introduced, `test_multiple_unknown_push_targets_emit_one_confirmation` and `test_unknown_push_target_does_not_prompt_before_merged_branch_block`, are absent from the test file.
  WHY: The batching defect (multiple JSON objects on stdout, ask-before-block on mixed targets) has no automated regression coverage.
- Requirement: The LAST RUN DIFF deferred every "could not resolve git push" warning into a single `unknown_destination_reasons` accumulator and emitted one `_request_confirmation` after the per-target loop, with bulk reasons funneled into the same list. The editor summary stated "A confirmed merged-branch block now takes priority, and multiple unknown targets produce one confirmation."
  Expected change site: `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` inside `_evaluate_bash` — three coordinated edits: (1) declare `unknown_destination_reasons: list[str] = []` after `bulk_reasons`, (2) change per-target branch from `_request_confirmation(target.warning)` to `unknown_destination_reasons.append(target.warning)`, (3) combine bulk and unknown reasons into one deferred `_request_confirmation`. Same edits in `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`.
  Evidence of absence: `unknown_destination_reasons` does not appear anywhere in the repository. `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1329` still calls `_request_confirmation(target.warning)` in the loop, and lines 1398-1402 still have the standalone bulk-reasons confirmation.
  severity=high | confidence=[5]
- Requirement: The LAST RUN DIFF committed two regression tests: `test_multiple_unknown_push_targets_emit_one_confirmation` (parametrized over `HEAD:$DEST1 HEAD:$DEST2` and `HEAD:$DEST1 :`) and `test_unknown_push_target_does_not_prompt_before_merged_branch_block` (asserting `code == 2`, `"feature/x" in message`, and no ask JSON on stdout).
  Expected change site: `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py` between `test_unknown_explicit_push_target_requires_confirmation` (ends line 989) and `test_cd_or_exit_preserves_worktree_for_push` (starts line 992).
  Evidence of absence: Neither function name appears in `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py` or anywhere in the repository. The test file jumps from line 989 directly to line 992 with no intervening test functions.
  severity=high | confidence=[5]
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1328-1330 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: `_evaluate_bash` calls `_request_confirmation` inside the per-target loop for any target with an unresolvable push destination.
  WHY: When a `git push` invocation contains multiple unknown targets, it writes multiple JSON objects to stdout; if an unresolvable target precedes a target pointing to an already-merged branch, it emits an ask before the merged-branch block.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1398-1402 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: Post-loop bulk-reasons handling calls `_request_confirmation` directly instead of coalescing with unknown-destination reasons into a single deferred confirmation.
  WHY: A push specifying both an unknown destination refspec and a bulk push flag can call `_request_confirmation` twice, outputting multiple JSON objects.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1328-1330, 1398-1402 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: `_evaluate_bash` calls `_request_confirmation` inside the per-target loop for unresolvable push destinations, and the post-loop bulk branch calls `_request_confirmation` separately.
  WHY: The workflow template must remain byte-identical to `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`; in consumer repos, this can print multiple JSON objects and emit an ask before evaluating a later merged-branch block.
- Requirement: When adding unknown explicit push destination handling and multi-target evaluation, regression tests must verify that commands with multiple unknown push targets emit a single confirmation decision and that an unknown target does not prompt before a merged branch block.
  Expected change site: `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py` after `test_unknown_explicit_push_target_requires_confirmation`
  Evidence of absence: In `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py`, `test_unknown_explicit_push_target_requires_confirmation` at line 983 is followed directly by `test_cd_or_exit_preserves_worktree_for_push` at line 992. The test file lacks `test_multiple_unknown_push_targets_emit_one_confirmation` and `test_unknown_push_target_does_not_prompt_before_merged_branch_block`, which were dropped du
